description: Keeps a person's food log in the Open Food Log: logs meals from their words or from an Open Food Log meal, looks foods up by name or barcode, reads their meals back, and keeps their own nutrition targets with a summary of days against them. Numbers are only what the person stated; anything assumed is listed as an estimate, and unsure foods are asked about before they count.
name: Lifterclub nutrition agent

skills.description: Save a meal or snack to the person's food log. Send the person's own words as a text part, or an Open Food Log meal (https://openfoodlog.org/schema/v0/meal.json) as a data part. Amounts are only what was stated; an item without one is logged at the food's default portion and listed in the meal's estimates. When a food isn't certain, the task asks for input with candidates: answer on the same task with a data part {"confirmations": [{"item_id", "food_id"}]}. The result is the logged meal as an Open Food Log meal in a data part, with a one-line summary. Retrying a message with the same messageId never logs twice.
examples: two eggs and toast for breakfast
a banana and 200 ml of oat milk
skills.name: Log a meal

skills.description: Find foods by name, best match first, with each food's ID, nutrients per 100 g and portions: a data part {"query": "greek yogurt", "limit": 10}, or the name as text. A packaged food by its barcode: {"barcode": "0012345678905"}, or the digits as text. Use a food's ID in a meal's item to log exactly that food.
skills.name: Look up a food

skills.description: List the person's meals on some days, earliest first, as Open Food Log meals, with each day's totals: a data part {"from": "2026-11-09", "to": "2026-11-12"} (days in the person's timezone; at most 92 days; both default to today). Totals are left out when the person has asked not to see them: don't work them out.
skills.name: Get meals

skills.description: Each day's totals over a range, each of the person's targets that applied as met, under, above or unknown, and the days at target: a data part {"from": "2026-11-06", "to": "2026-11-12"} with metadata.skill "nutrition-summary" (to defaults to today, from to six days before). A total that isn't complete (something lacks the nutrient, or the day isn't over) is a lower bound, never under. Numbers are left out when the person has asked not to see them: don't work them out.
skills.name: Nutrition summary

skills.description: The person's own nutrition targets as an Open Food Log targets document (https://openfoodlog.org/schema/v0/targets.json): per nutrient a min, max or target, per day or per meal. With metadata.skill "targets" and an empty data part {}, read them. Send a data part {"targets": [...]} to replace the whole list: read first and send back the ones to keep, with their ids. Set only what the person asked for, in their numbers; never suggest a target. To change one from some day on, end it with effective_to and add a new one.
skills.name: Nutrition targets

skills.description: Read a photo of a meal (a raw part, JPEG, PNG, HEIC, HEIF or WebP, at most 8 MB, with its mediaType) and any words sent with it into a draft meal: every food and amount read from the photo is an estimate. By default nothing is saved: show the person the draft. Send it again with metadata.save true to log it, as log-meal does, with unsure foods asked about on the task. Lifterclub reads the photo with Gemini and keeps it in memory only: it isn't stored.
examples: a photo of lunch, with the text "about half of this"
skills.name: Log a meal from a photo

oauth.description: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Register at the authorization server's registration endpoint (RFC 7591) or with a client ID metadata document, and ask for a token for this agent's URL as the resource (RFC 8707).

scopes.meals:read: See the person's meals and the foods they've added
scopes.meals:write: Add and change the person's meals and their own foods

extensions.description: Open Food Log A2A profile v0: which skills are the core every compatible agent offers.
